items.note: A yellow header band with a soft sagging arc opens the page, then cream filter pills with category dots and the selected ink pill with its white dot, and a 4-up grid of cream cards with saturated flat covers. Hierarchy and the warm neutral base are as clear as reference 01/02. The band's art is a generic sparkle, a pink disc and a cloud rather than a composition about the subject, and it is thinner than the reference's sparkle-and-cloud compositions.

A compact header with an ink cart pill and a cream menu circle, then a stacked yellow band with an arc, scrolling filter pills and one-column cream cards. It is close to reference 04's phone stack. The band's lead is squeezed into a narrow left column and wraps to four ragged lines, where the reference uses the full width.

The night palette works as in reference 03: navy page, indigo cards and pills, a white selected pill and a white cart pill. The yellow band and the flat covers keep their hues. As in light mode, the band's art is the same generic disc, cloud and sparkle.

Navy phone screen with a white cart pill, an indigo menu circle and indigo filter pills on ledges. It is convincingly the derived night look. The header band's lead again wraps narrowly to four lines with a one-word last line.

A green header band (the area hue) with breadcrumb, h2 title and arc; a large green cover panel beside the price, bordered choice rows with small glyphs, cream stepper circles, a blue add-to-cart pill and a cream details panel with a spot plate. This is the system's recipe, well executed. The cover repeats the band's green, so two big green fields stack, and the band art is again the stock disc, cloud and sparkle.

The green band, full-width choice rows with glyphs and the full-width blue pill are well built. The product cover is pushed below the details panel to the end of the page, so the phone screen shows no picture of the product. That is weaker hierarchy than the reference, whose phone hero keeps its imagery up front.

Night version: green band, indigo choice rows with a white selected border, indigo stepper circles and a blue add-to-cart pill. It translates cleanly, like reference 03. The same doubled green field and generic band art appear as in light mode.
Navy phone screen with the green band, indigo choice rows and a blue pill. It is crafted well, but the product cover again comes last, after the details panel, so the item is never seen near the top.

An orange band with dark on-field text, a stacked-pill pictogram on an orange cover, size choice rows each with a different orange glyph, and a blue pill. The area hue is applied consistently, as reference 05/10 would. The cover and band are the same orange, and the band art is the same disc, cloud and sparkle as every other page.

The orange band with its arc, the stacked size rows and the full-width blue pill all read as the system. The product cover sits below the details panel at the bottom, and the band's lead wraps to three short lines.

Navy page, orange band and cover, indigo size rows with the white selected border, and a blue pill. It is close to the derived night language, with the same generic band art and the same hue doubling as the light version.
Navy phone screen with the orange band, a large price and indigo size rows with glyphs. It is well built, but as on the other product phones the cover is moved to the end of the page.

A blue header band for the cart area, then a wide cream empty-state panel with a tiny two-dot mark, an h4 title, one line and an ink pill, then a cream footer with a rise arc. The structure follows the spec, but the empty state is far thinner than the reference's spot compositions (07, 09), so the screen reads sparse and generic.

A blue band with a yellow disc, a cream empty-state panel with a small blue-and-yellow dot pair and an ink pill, and a cream footer arc. The language is present, but the empty state carries almost no illustration, compared with the reference's plated pictograms.

Night version: blue band, an indigo empty panel with a white pill and an indigo footer arc. The dark translation is clean, but the empty state's lone two-dot mark leaves the large panel feeling unfinished next to the reference.
Navy phone screen with the blue band, an indigo empty panel, a small dot mark and a white pill. It matches the light layout and carries the same weak empty-state illustration.

findings.summary: On phones the product-detail cover is treated as decorative art and moved below the details to the end of the page, so the item is never pictured near the top. The reference keeps its hero imagery up front on mobile.
findings.promptFix: In Layout adaptation, say that an image or cover that represents the item itself (a product, a listing, a profile, a document) is content, not art: on narrow screens it stays directly after the title, scaled down if needed. Only decorative shapes, confetti and compositions move last.
findings.specRule: Priority on narrow screens: title and primary action first, data next, art last

findings.summary: Every header band carries the same three pieces (a disc, a cloud and a sparkle) whatever the area. On product pages the cover panel repeats the band's hue, so two large same-hue fields stack in one viewport. The reference's art is composed per section and keeps a single dominant field.

The empty state is a large cream panel with only a small two-dot mark. The reference illustrates such moments with a plated or composed flat-shape scene (and the spec asks for a full-size composition or large glyph), so the screen reads bare.

On phones the header band keeps a wide reserved art column, so its lead wraps to three or four short lines ending in a lone word. The reference's phone band lets text use the full width, with art behind the trailing edge.
